sources.why: FAA rules page; sets the 100/160 Wh limits but recommends no product
sources.evidence: Rechargeable batteries with a capacity of 0-100 Wh are allowed on passenger aircraft, while those with a capacity of 101-160 Wh require approval from the air carrier

sources.why: FAA PackSafe entry on spare batteries; rules only, no picks or prices
sources.evidence: Lithium ion (rechargeable) batteries are limited to a rating of 100 watt hours (Wh) per battery.

sources.why: FAA blog on packing hazmat; restates limits, nothing on which bank to buy
sources.evidence: Spare lithium batteries, including power banks, must never be in checked bags.

sources.why: Southwest policy page; one-bank, 100 Wh, under-seat rules, no products
sources.evidence: each Customer is limited to one power bank (effective April 20, 2026) must be carried in the cabin; must not be placed in checked luggage must not exceed 100 watt-hours

sources.why: TSA list served through an iframe proxy; no text reached the model
IATA operator guidance PDF on the March 2026 ICAO addendum; regulatory, no consumer picks
sources.evidence: The addendum provides for passengers to carry power banks of 100 -160 Wh with the approval of the operator; however, given the concerns with regulatory oversight of power bank manufacturers

sources.why: AP news explainer on the rules and incidents; names no power bank
sources.evidence: The most important thing to know is that you can’t pack lithium battery chargers in your checked luggage. They need to go in your carry-on luggage.

sources.why: American Airlines restricted-items page; a generic notice, no Wh detail or products
sources.evidence: Large portable power banks and lithium-ion battery-powered generators are not allowed as carry-on or checked items.

sources.why: Travel blog explainer on checking your bank's Wh; no models, prices or testing
sources.evidence: Count, storage and use limits are the airline's own, so a bank that clears security can still be refused at check-in or the gate.

missing: An actual product pick: specific sub-100 Wh power banks (ideally ~60-99 Wh, 20-27k mAh) with the Wh rating printed on the casing so gate agents accept them, current prices and codes, and a note on which airlines now cap you at one bank or ban in-flight charging.
why: Every result is a rules page (FAA x3, IATA, Southwest, American, AP, a travel blog, an unreadable TSA proxy) answering the neighbouring question "what do airlines allow"; none names, tests or prices a power bank, so no major reviewer or authority answers the shopper's "best power bank" question. The FAA/IATA pages will keep the rules citations, but a focused page that lists compliant, Wh-labelled banks with current prices and a direct pick would be the only product source in the set.
